mechanism.reading: pf's stat forecast responds to its own minutes forecast with elasticity ~0.7 (rate slope ~-0.3); D (minutes x rate) is fully elastic and A is minutes-free but near zero weight, so the shortfall sits in the LightGBM rung E. Actual per-minute rates do not rise when minutes fall, so pf over-forecasts when it cuts minutes. This is a coherence defect of the stack, not a basketball effect.

limitations: Same one-month window as 0.3 (TEST = 88 games, two cohorts of about a week). A validated row means the contract rule passed on this window only.
The mechanism is read from the frozen forecasts and the owner's model source; the production stack itself was not re-run (its LightGBM rung has no archived inputs).
Component switches and weights are chosen on the 2026-27 TRAIN window (about 1,980 played rows, 88 games); grids were fixed before the TEST read.
The W grid was widened to 0..1 relative to 0.3 because 0.3's weight sat on its 0.5 edge; this is a design change made after 0.3's result was known and is disclosed.
Spread and total probabilities use pf's normal approximation with the archived rho; a common shift of both teams leaves spreads unchanged.
No new external data was collected. No fees, no execution, no profitability claim.

verdict.evidence_sufficiency: 88 TEST games in two cohorts of about one week (the same window as 0.3); one month of one season
verdict.reason: 4 of 7 headline rows validated against the frozen production forecasts; vs 0.3 better on none, worse on ['player_rebounds']; significantly worse than the Kalshi T-60 mid on ['player_points']
verdict.rule: contract.verdict_from on every row (95% game-clustered CI below zero, Holm p < 0.05, same sign in both TEST cohorts). Overall VALIDATED_IMPROVEMENT only if every headline row (vs frozen pf) is validated AND the challenger is not significantly worse than the Kalshi T-60 mid on any family.
